newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares to bounce from ex-dividend dip.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares to bounce from ex-dividend dip.

text.p: Leading Belgian shares ended mixed on Wednesday although dividend payments knocked the feet from under several large issues, dragging the blue chip Bel-20 index down 17.20 points, or 0.76 percent, to 2,258.12.
Dividend payments by Delhaize, PetroFina, Electrabel, SGB and Barco had been due to take 16 points off the index.

Barco was the only one of the four to end the day in positive territory, adding 10 francs to 6,340 francs. Overall, 10 Bel-20 issues lost ground, nine were higher and one, cement maker CBR was unchanged at 3,355 francs.

Traders said, however, they believed underlying sentiment remained positive despite fears over economic and monetary union (EMU) linked to Sunday's French elections, which hit bond markets and knocked 3.63 percent off the CAC-40.

"The market will go higher. As long as the dividend period is not behind us there is little danger of a spectacular break down," one Ghent-based trader said. "Any weakness is a buying opportunity as far as I'm concerned."
Dealers said PetroFina was one share that would rise because its controlling shareholder, the Groupe Bruxelles Lambert group, was keen to see warrants on its shares exercised.
The more than one million warrants give holders the right to one new PetroFina share at a price of 12,500 francs and can be exercised until June 3.
PetroFina is hoping to raise up to 14.5 billion francs from the warrants to buy out minorities in its U.S. Fina unit.
One trader, however, believed the warrants were "heading to zero", meaning few investors were interested in exercising the option. The warrants ended Wednesday down 21 francs at 16 francs.

Among small caps Tubize A continued its spectacular ascent despite a fall in main asset UCB. Tubize A rose 2,500 francs to 367,500 francs, up nearly 40 percent on the year. Blue chip UCB, a niche player in chemicals and drugs, lost 1,300 francs to 95,700.

One trader said he was not aware of any reason for the rise, noting normally Tubize A falls or rises in tandem with UCB, in which it owns an indirect 22 percent stake, held via listed holding company Financieres d'Obourg.
